content: Before starting flibanserin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you have any liver problems. Additionally, provide them with a complete list of all the products you use, including prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, and herbal supplements. Flibanserin is not intended to treat low sexual desire caused by medical or mental health conditions, relationship issues, or the effects of other medications. This medication is not suitable for women who have gone through menopause or for men. Read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist before you begin taking flibanserin and each time you get a refill. Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor, typically once daily at bedtime. It is crucial to take flibanserin only at bedtime to minimize the risk of low blood pressure, fainting, and drowsiness while awake. After taking flibanserin, avoid consuming alcohol until the next day. Do not eat grapefruit or drink grapefruit juice while using this medication unless your doctor or pharmacist confirms it is safe to do so, as grapefruit can increase the likelihood of side effects. Take this medication consistently to achieve the maximum benefit. Common side effects may include drowsiness, dizziness, nausea, or fatigue. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, low blood pressure and fainting may still occur, even when flibanserin is taken alone. These risks increase if you take the medication with alcohol, less than two hours after consuming alcohol, at a time other than bedtime, or in doses higher than prescribed. If you feel dizzy or lightheaded, lie down immediately. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, seek emergency medical attention by calling 911. For non-emergency overdoses, contact a poison control center immediately. In the U.S., call 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at bedtime the following day. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store flibanserin at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, following your pharmacist's instructions. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness for at least six hours after taking flibanserin, as it may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Alcohol and marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects, so avoid consuming them while using this medication. During pregnancy, flibanserin should only be used if clearly necessary. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk, but due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using flibanserin. Drug interactions may alter how flibanserin works or increase the risk of serious side effects. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements. Certain medications, such as azole antifungals (e.g., fluconazole, ketoconazole), calcium channel blockers (e.g., diltiazem, verapamil), macrolide antibiotics (e.g., clarithromycin, erythromycin), nefazodone, rifamycins (e.g., rifabutin, rifampin), and ritonavir, can affect the removal of flibanserin from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Check the labels of all your medications, including allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. This information is not exhaustive and does not guarantee that flibanserin is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
